slides.headline: One door. One night before the battle.
slides.sub: John Everett Millais, The Black Brunswicker, 1860

slides.headline: Brussels, 1815
slides.text: Brussels, June 1815. Napoleon's army is close. That night, at the Duchess of Richmond's ball, officers are called away to fight.

slides.headline: The soldier
slides.text: He wears the black uniform of the Brunswick troops, with its silver skull badge. His regiment marches at first light.

slides.headline: The door
slides.text: He pulls the door open, ready to leave. She pushes it shut with her hand. For a moment, neither of them lets go.

slides.headline: Her
slides.text: She is still in her ballgown, pressing against him, eyes lowered. She cannot ask him to stay, but she won't let him go.

slides.headline: The dog
slides.text: At their feet, her little dog with a red ribbon looks up at them both. Even it seems to know.

slides.headline: On the wall
slides.text: On the wall hangs a print of Napoleon crossing the Alps. The enemy he must go and fight is already in the room.

slides.headline: The models
slides.text: The woman was Kate, the daughter of Charles Dickens. The soldier posed separately. The two models never actually met.

slides.headline: Quatre Bras
slides.text: The next day, at Quatre Bras, the Duke of Brunswick himself was killed. Millais never tells us if this soldier came back. Did he?
